summary: Intermittent reserved-capacity throughput degradation correlated with migratory tenant short-burst loads
description:
Issue summary: NovaChat is seeing repeated, short-lived p95/p99 throughput collapses in their reserved GPU pool. Impact: customer traffic experiences bursts of 10–30s elevated latencies and throughput drops (~50% p99 increase) multiple times per hour causing degraded user-facing features.
Environment: Dedicated reserved pool (pool-425) in prod-us-east serving NovaChat's routes. Customer reports started 2026-03-09 09:12 UTC.
Timeline: 2026-03-09: initial alerting from monitoring. 2026-03-10: support ticket opened. 2026-03-11: SRE observed correlating spikes with a tenant running short-lived high-concurrency streams and a scheduled nightly checkpoint on another tenant. 2026-03-12: mitigation runbooks applied.
Observed behavior: sudden increase in queue depth on GPU worker daemons, NVLink utilization spikes to ~95%, ephemeral evictions of small in-flight batches, autoscaler temporarily requests additional nodes but allocation lags leading to throughput degradation. Expected behavior: stable throughput with autoscaler smoothing short bursts without p99 degradation.
Impact classification: Customer-facing P1 (repeated user-visible latency spikes).
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate 200 concurrent short streams (avg 300 tokens) against a single tenant in a dedicated pool with small batch sizes enabled
Run a second concurrent tenant that triggers a checkpoint/IO-heavy background job at the same time
Observe p95/p99 and GPU NVLink utilization on the pool over 60s window
logs_and_metrics: excerpt: worker-42: queue_depth spike from 12->86 at 2026-03-11T02:14:12Z
autoscaler: scale_request at 02:14:20Z -> new nodes provisioned at 02:18:37Z (4m17s provisioning lag)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial hypothesis: slot fragmentation from many small streams. Verified increased worker queue lengths and slot serialization.
2026-03-11: Observed NVLink saturation coincident with a different tenant's scheduled checkpoint writer. NVLink high utilization causes kernel slowdown for all GPUs in node.
2026-03-11: Autoscaler metrics show burst below allocation threshold due to smoothing policy; scale decision delayed 20–30s to avoid thrash — in this case delay contributed to observed p99 increases.

2026-03-12: Reproduced with synthetic workload in staging; root causes composite: (1) short-stream fanout causing slot fragmentation, (2) NVLink IO burst from checkpoint writer on co-located tenant, (3) autoscaler smoothing parameters too conservative for short bursts.
resolution: Workarounds applied: (1) temporarily reserved 2 extra standby nodes for pool-425 assigned to NovaChat (manual allocation) to absorb bursts; (2) moved the checkpointing tenant to a different reserved pool during customer business hours; (3) suggested NovaChat reduce concurrency of small short streams as short-term mitigation. Permanent follow-ups: autoscaler tuning PR (see related_github_prs) to detect 'short-burst' pattern and apply faster transient scale-up; implement NVLink-aware placement constraint to avoid co-locating heavy IO jobs with latency-sensitive tenants; add detection alert for 'NVLink+queue spike' pattern and a runbook. Status: mitigation reduced p99 spikes by ~80% during observed windows; work ongoing to deploy autoscaler change and placement constraints (ETA: 2026-04-02).
